title: The valley of webhooks
excerpt: I've built the same webhook consumer three times at three companies. The fourth time, I want a better primitive.
content_html:
The third time

I’ve built the same system three times now, at three different companies, for three different providers. It never has a name and it never appears on a roadmap, but it always goes the same way: the truth about your own customers lives in someone else’s database. The users live in an identity provider, the subscriptions in Stripe, the bounces in whatever sends your email, and your product needs that truth locally. So you subscribe to webhooks and keep a copy.

The first time, I thought I was building an endpoint: one route that parses the JSON and updates a row, an afternoon of work.

The afternoon grew into a week. First came signature verification, because an open endpoint that mutates your database is a hole. Then the dedup table, because deliveries arrive twice and the docs cheerfully call this “at-least-once.” Then the handler got a buffer, because a membership.created sometimes shows up before the user.created it points to. Then the bootstrap importer, because webhooks only tell you what happens after you subscribe, and it raced the live events, so it grew a locking scheme. And finally came the reconciliation cron: a job that crawls the provider’s list APIs at 3 a.m., diffs them against our tables, and quietly fixes what disagrees.

I want to be honest about what that cron is. It’s a written confession. It says: I do not trust the copy I built, and I have no way to know when it’s wrong, so I will re-derive it from scratch every night, forever.

The trust was gone for a reason. The drift never announces itself; ours was found by a support ticket. A customer had cancelled months earlier and our database still said active; some customer.subscription.deleted had evaporated between Stripe and us, and nothing anywhere was capable of noticing: not their dashboard, which showed the delivery as retried and eventually dropped, and not our logs, which cannot log a request that never arrived.

And that’s only the code. Every provider also brings its own dashboard. Three providers, three webhook configuration pages, each with its own idea of how endpoints are registered, which events exist, how test and live environments are kept apart, and where the signing secret lives. When something breaks, debugging is a tour: their delivery log in one tab, our logs in another, and a third tab for whichever dashboard I currently suspect. None of them look alike, and all of them have to be checked.

By the third time I built this system, I had stopped pretending. I budgeted for the whole stack up front (signatures, dedup, buffering, bootstrap, cron) and somewhere in the middle of writing my third dedup table, I finally asked the question I should have asked the first time.

What exactly am I reconstructing here?

Notifications aren’t data

I was reconstructing an ordered log. Every one of those integrations was an attempt to turn a stream of notifications back into the ordered, complete, current history it came from.

And here’s the absurd part: that history exists. It has to, because it’s sitting inside the provider; it’s how they render their dashboards, their event pages, and their webhook replay tools. The provider takes their ordered log, shreds it into individual HTTP POSTs, fires them at my endpoint over a channel that guarantees neither order nor delivery, and then I reassemble the log on my side. So does every other consumer, independently, each with their own bugs.

It’s a jigsaw puzzle where the manufacturer had the original picture, cut it up, mailed me the pieces one at a time, lost a few in the post, mailed some twice, and printed nothing on the box. And when my assembled puzzle doesn’t match the original, their support team asks me which pieces I’m missing. I don’t know, and that’s the entire problem: nothing announces a gap.

None of this is any provider’s bug. Their webhooks work exactly as documented. The problem is what a webhook is: a notification, “something happened, here’s a POST about it.” Notifications are a fine way to trigger a side effect and a terrible way to transfer a dataset, and somewhere along the way we started using them for the second thing without noticing we’d changed jobs.

How did this become the norm?

Nobody decided this. The term “webhook” was coined by Jeff Lindsay in 2007, and the early uses were genuinely good fits: GitHub’s post-receive hooks kicking off a CI build, or a payment event pinging your server so it could email a receipt. The job was to do a thing when a thing happens, and for that a POST is perfect: fire-and-forget is fine when forgetting is fine.

Webhooks spread because they were the cheapest thing a provider could ship (one HTTP POST) and the cheapest thing a consumer could receive (you already had a web server, so you just added a route). By the early 2010s, “we have webhooks” was a checkbox on every API’s landing page, and the checkbox never distinguished between two very different jobs:

  1. Trigger a side effect: send the receipt, start the build, ping the channel.
  2. Keep a copy of the provider’s data correct: this customer deleted their payment method, so update it in your DB too.

Job one is what webhooks were born for. Job two is what I was doing all three times, and job two is the one where every property webhooks lack (ordering, completeness, bootstrap, verifiability) is precisely the property you need.

We picked the tool that was lying on the table in 2007, and then we spent fifteen years compensating.

The valley

There’s a concept in evolutionary biology I can’t stop thinking about: the fitness landscape. Peaks are good designs, valleys are bad ones, and populations climb whatever slope they happen to be standing on. The trap is the local optimum: a small hill that’s better than its immediate surroundings, so evolution parks there, even when a much higher peak exists across the valley. Getting to the higher peak means crossing through designs that are temporarily worse, and evolution doesn’t do temporarily worse.

Webhooks-for-replication are a local optimum, and the proof is the pile of workarounds on the valley floor: signature schemes, dedup stores, idempotent handlers, retry queues with exponential backoff on the provider side and dead-letter queues behind them, webhook logs with replay tooling because consumers keep asking for replays, and my 3 a.m. cron.

The pile has an economy on top of it. Svix exists so providers don’t have to build webhook delivery; Hookdeck exists so consumers don’t have to build webhook ingestion. AWS will sell you the valley as managed services, with EventBridge to ingest your SaaS partners’ events, SQS to queue them, and Lambda to retry your handler, and you get to assemble the pipeline yourself. And an entire industry of connector platforms (Fivetran, Airbyte, every “unified API” startup) is, at bottom, pseudo-CDC: change data capture reconstructed from webhooks and polled list APIs, one bespoke connector at a time, sold as a product. Inside a database, capturing changes is a solved problem: it’s called replication, and it works because there’s a log. Between companies, we rebuild it out of doorbells.

My favorite workaround of them all is the local tunnel. Many providers ship a CLI like stripe listen that opens a tunnel to your laptop, because a webhook cannot reach localhost. Think about what that is: a product, built and maintained by the provider, reinvented multiple times, whose entire purpose is to work around the delivery direction of their own primitive. When multiple providers all need to ship a local tunnel so developers can develop, the primitive is answering the wrong question.

None of this tooling is bad engineering; it’s excellent engineering. That’s what a local optimum looks like: so much excellent engineering poured into the valley floor that the valley becomes comfortable, and nobody looks up.

But some providers have looked up. Stripe retains thirty days of events and exposes /v1/events, an ordered, listable log, and recommends reconciling against it. WorkOS ships an Events API, an ordered cursor-paginated log, and their own docs recommend it over webhooks when data consistency matters. The log keeps escaping, and each escape mints its own bespoke cursor semantics, its own bootstrap story, no way to verify a replica, and no shared contract, but the direction is unmistakable. This is convergent evolution: unrelated organisms, same environmental pressure, same wing.

The log exists everywhere, but the contract doesn’t.

Could it be better?

Before reaching for a new design, it’s worth asking what any replacement would actually have to provide. My three integrations suggest the list: order, so changes can be applied without buffering; a way to start from nothing, so bootstrap isn’t a separate import racing the live events; deletes as data, so absence stops being the failure mode; resumability, so my downtime is my problem instead of a data-loss event; and some way to verify the result, so trust doesn’t decay into a 3 a.m. cron.

Measured against that list, the obvious candidates come up short. Polling the list APIs harder is the reconciliation cron promoted to a whole strategy: it can rebuild current state, but it burns rate limits discovering that mostly nothing changed, it says nothing about order, and a deleted object looks identical to an object that never existed. Managed delivery, whether that’s Svix on the provider’s side or EventBridge and SQS on mine, makes the pushes more reliable, but they are still pushes: still no bootstrap, still no verification, still notifications pretending to be a dataset. That path hardens the valley floor without climbing anywhere.

The third candidate is the one the providers keep half-building on their own: stop pushing altogether, and let the consumer read the log itself.

Flip the arrow

So here’s the thought experiment. What if instead of the provider telling us when there is new information, we ask the provider what new information it has for us since we last checked?

Suppose a provider served one URL per collection, and that URL returned an ordered, cursor-addressed change log of full-state events. Ask without a cursor and you read from the beginning, which is your bootstrap, with no separate import and no race. Ask with a cursor and you resume where you left off. Your entire sync state is that cursor.

GET /feed/customers?cursor=01J9XQ4R
Prefer: stream

200 OK
Content-Type: application/x-ndjson

{"cursor":"01J9XR2M","operation":"upsert","object":{"id":"cus_123","plan":"pro"}}
{"cursor":"01J9XR2N","operation":"delete","object_id":"cus_099"}

Send Prefer: stream and the response never ends: each change arrives as it commits, over a connection you opened, using the same API key you use for the normal REST endpoints. Leave it off and you get a bounded page you can poll from a cron. It’s the same endpoint, the same events, the same cursors, and the same consumer code.

None of this is exotic; it’s a paginated GET. But walk back through my afternoon-that-grew and watch what it does to the stack:

  • The dedup table is gone. Every event carries the object’s full current state, so applying one is a blind upsert keyed by id, and the same event applied twice produces the same result.
  • The ordering buffer is gone, because the log is ordered.
  • The bootstrap importer and its locking scheme are gone. A new consumer reads the same feed with no cursor, replays the collection, and carries straight on into live changes in one request.
  • The lost delete is impossible. A tombstone is an event in the log, and it sits there until I read it. My cancelled customer cannot silently stay active, because absence stopped being the failure mode.
  • The endpoint, the signatures, and the tunnel never exist in the first place. Every connection is consumer-initiated, and the loop runs behind NAT, on a laptop, or in a scheduled job.

The feed could carry one more thing. When a read reaches the end of the log, the provider could tell you what should be there: a count and a checksum of current state, at the cursor you now hold. You compare the two, and you know your replica is right instead of assuming it. My 3 a.m. cron, the written confession, becomes a comparison I’ve already made by the time I would have thought to schedule one.

The fourth time

If a feed like that existed, the fourth time I build this system would be a loop: GET the feed, let “upsert” upsert the object into my db and “delete” delete it, and save the last cursor. That’s twenty lines with no route, no secrets to rotate, no queue, and no cron. The replica carries its own proof of correctness, and when someone asks which customers have an active subscription and a bouncing email address, the answer is a JOIN across local tables with no silent asterisk attached.

Nobody serves this today. That’s the catch, and it’s also the point.

I wanted to see whether the idea survives being written down precisely, so I drafted it as a protocol: SCROLL, short for Synchronized Change Replication Over Line Logs, at welidev.github.io/scroll. It’s draft-00 in the request-for-comments sense of the phrase. It pins down the feed, the cursors, the streaming and polling modes, the checkpoints, tombstones, and retention, and it marks the places where my own confidence is lowest. It also doesn’t require waiting for providers, since a shim can synthesize a feed from any provider’s existing webhooks and list APIs, which is how I plan to find out where the design is wrong.

If you’ve lived in the valley, if you’ve written a dedup table or debugged a reconciliation cron or watched a delete evaporate, read it and tell me where it breaks. Disagreement is the desired response; silence is the failure mode.

sentences.zh: 漂移永远不会自行显现；我们是通过支持票找到的。

sentences.en: A customer had cancelled months earlier and our database still said active; some customer.subscription.deleted had evaporated between Stripe and us, and nothing anywhere was capable of noticing: not their dashboard, which showed the delivery as retried and eventually dropped, and not our logs, which cannot log a request that never arrived.
sentences.zh: 一位客户在几个月前取消了订单，而我们的数据库仍然显示处于活动状态；一些 customer.subscription.deleted 在 Stripe 和我们之间消失了，任何地方都没有注意到：不是他们的仪表板，它显示了重试并最终丢弃的交付，也不是我们的日志，它无法记录从未到达的请求。

blocks.html_en: And that’s only the code. Every provider also brings its own dashboard. Three providers, three webhook configuration pages, each with its own idea of how endpoints are registered, which events exist, how test and live environments are kept apart, and where the signing secret lives. When something breaks, debugging is a tour: their delivery log in one tab, our logs in another, and a third tab for whichever dashboard I currently suspect. None of them look alike, and all of them have to be checked.

sentences.en: And that’s only the code.
sentences.zh: 这只是代码。

sentences.en: Every provider also brings its own dashboard.
sentences.zh: 每个提供商还自带自己的仪表板。

sentences.en: Three providers, three webhook configuration pages, each with its own idea of how endpoints are registered, which events exist, how test and live environments are kept apart, and where the signing secret lives.
sentences.zh: 三个提供程序、三个 Webhook 配置页面，每个页面都有自己的想法：如何注册端点、存在哪些事件、如何分隔测试和实时环境以及签名秘密所在的位置。

sentences.en: When something breaks, debugging is a tour: their delivery log in one tab, our logs in another, and a third tab for whichever dashboard I currently suspect.
sentences.zh: 当出现问题时，调试就是一次游览：他们的交付日志在一个选项卡中，我们的日志在另一个选项卡中，第三个选项卡用于我当前怀疑的仪表板。

sentences.en: None of them look alike, and all of them have to be checked.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来都不一样，都必须进行检查。

blocks.html_en: By the third time I built this system, I had stopped pretending. I budgeted for the whole stack up front (signatures, dedup, buffering, bootstrap, cron) and somewhere in the middle of writing my third dedup table, I finally asked the question I should have asked the first time.

sentences.en: By the third time I built this system, I had stopped pretending.
sentences.zh: 当我第三次构建这个系统时，我已经不再假装了。

sentences.en: I budgeted for the whole stack up front (signatures, dedup, buffering, bootstrap, cron) and somewhere in the middle of writing my third dedup table, I finally asked the question I should have asked the first time.
sentences.zh: 我预先对整个堆栈进行了预算（签名、重复数据删除、缓冲、引导程序、cron），在编写第三个重复数据删除表的过程中，我终于问了我应该第一次问的问题。

blocks.html_en: What exactly am I reconstructing here?

sentences.en: What exactly am I reconstructing here?
sentences.zh: 我到底要在这里重建什么？

blocks.html_en: Notifications aren’t data

sentences.en: Notifications aren’t data
sentences.zh: 通知不是数据

blocks.html_en: I was reconstructing an ordered log. Every one of those integrations was an attempt to turn a stream of notifications back into the ordered, complete, current history it came from.

sentences.en: I was reconstructing an ordered log.
sentences.zh: 我正在重建一个有序的日志。

sentences.en: Every one of those integrations was an attempt to turn a stream of notifications back into the ordered, complete, current history it came from.
sentences.zh: 这些集成中的每一个都试图将通知流转回其来源的有序、完整、当前的历史记录。

blocks.html_en: And here’s the absurd part: that history exists. It has to, because it’s sitting inside the provider; it’s how they render their dashboards, their event pages, and their webhook replay tools. The provider takes their ordered log, shreds it into individual HTTP POSTs, fires them at my endpoint over a channel that guarantees neither order nor delivery, and then I reassemble the log on my side. So does every other consumer, independently, each with their own bugs.

sentences.en: And here’s the absurd part: that history exists.
sentences.zh: 这是荒谬的部分：历史存在。

sentences.en: It has to, because it’s sitting inside the provider; it’s how they render their dashboards, their event pages, and their webhook replay tools.
sentences.zh: 它必须如此，因为它位于提供者内部；这就是他们呈现仪表板、事件页面和 Webhook 重播工具的方式。

sentences.en: The provider takes their ordered log, shreds it into individual HTTP POSTs, fires them at my endpoint over a channel that guarantees neither order nor delivery, and then I reassemble the log on my side.
sentences.zh: 提供者获取他们有序的日志，将其粉碎成单独的 HTTP POST，通过既不保证顺序也不保证交付的通道在我的端点处触发它们，然后我在我这边重新组装日志。

sentences.en: So does every other consumer, independently, each with their own bugs.
sentences.zh: 其他每个独立的消费者也是如此，每个人都有自己的错误。

blocks.html_en: It’s a jigsaw puzzle where the manufacturer had the original picture, cut it up, mailed me the pieces one at a time, lost a few in the post, mailed some twice, and printed nothing on the box. And when my assembled puzzle doesn’t match the original, their support team asks me which pieces I’m missing. I don’t know, and that’s the entire problem: nothing announces a gap.

sentences.en: It’s a jigsaw puzzle where the manufacturer had the original picture, cut it up, mailed me the pieces one at a time, lost a few in the post, mailed some twice, and printed nothing on the box.
sentences.zh: 这是一个拼图游戏，制造商有原始图片，将其剪碎，一次邮寄给我一块，在邮寄过程中丢失了一些，邮寄了两次，并且在盒子上没有打印任何内容。

sentences.en: And when my assembled puzzle doesn’t match the original, their support team asks me which pieces I’m missing.
sentences.zh: 当我组装的拼图与原始拼图不匹配时，他们的支持团队会问我缺少哪些拼图。

sentences.en: I don’t know, and that’s the entire problem: nothing announces a gap.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，这就是整个问题：没有任何东西表明存在差距。

blocks.html_en: None of this is any provider’s bug. Their webhooks work exactly as documented. The problem is what a webhook is: a notification, “something happened, here’s a POST about it.” Notifications are a fine way to trigger a side effect and a terrible way to transfer a dataset, and somewhere along the way we started using them for the second thing without noticing we’d changed jobs.

sentences.en: None of this is any provider’s bug.
sentences.zh: 这些都不是任何提供商的错误。

sentences.en: Their webhooks work exactly as documented.
sentences.zh: 他们的 webhook 的工作方式与记录的完全一样。

sentences.en: The problem is what a webhook is: a notification, “something happened, here’s a POST about it.”
sentences.zh: 问题在于 webhook 是什么：一个通知，“发生了一些事情，这里有一个关于它的帖子。”

sentences.en: Notifications are a fine way to trigger a side effect and a terrible way to transfer a dataset, and somewhere along the way we started using them for the second thing without noticing we’d changed jobs.
sentences.zh: 通知是触发副作用的好方法，也是传输数据集的糟糕方法，在我们开始将它们用于第二件事的过程中，我们没有注意到我们已经换了工作。

blocks.html_en: How did this become the norm?

sentences.en: How did this become the norm?
sentences.zh: 这如何成为常态？

blocks.html_en: Nobody decided this. The term “webhook” was coined by Jeff Lindsay in 2007, and the early uses were genuinely good fits: GitHub’s post-receive hooks kicking off a CI build, or a payment event pinging your server so it could email a receipt. The job was to do a thing when a thing happens, and for that a POST is perfect: fire-and-forget is fine when forgetting is fine.

sentences.en: Nobody decided this.
sentences.zh: 没有人决定这个。

sentences.en: The term “webhook” was coined by Jeff Lindsay in 2007, and the early uses were genuinely good fits: GitHub’s post-receive hooks kicking off a CI build, or a payment event pinging your server so it could email a receipt.
sentences.zh: “webhook”这个术语是由 Jeff Lindsay 在 2007 年创造的，早期的用途确实很合适：GitHub 的 post-receive hooks 启动 CI 构建，或者支付事件 ping 您的服务器，以便它可以通过电子邮件发送收据。

sentences.en: The job was to do a thing when a thing happens, and for that a POST is perfect: fire-and-forget is fine when forgetting is fine.
sentences.zh: 我们的工作是在事情发生时做一件事，为此，POST 是完美的：当忘记可以时，即发即忘也可以。

blocks.html_en: Webhooks spread because they were the cheapest thing a provider could ship (one HTTP POST) and the cheapest thing a consumer could receive (you already had a web server, so you just added a route). By the early 2010s, “we have webhooks” was a checkbox on every API’s landing page, and the checkbox never distinguished between two very different jobs:

sentences.en: Webhooks spread because they were the cheapest thing a provider could ship (one HTTP POST) and the cheapest thing a consumer could receive (you already had a web server, so you just added a route).
sentences.zh: Webhook 之所以能够传播，是因为它们是提供商可以运送的最便宜的东西（一个 HTTP POST），也是消费者可以接收的最便宜的东西（您已经有一个 Web 服务器，所以您只需添加一条路由）。

sentences.en: By the early 2010s, “we have webhooks” was a checkbox on every API’s landing page, and the checkbox never distinguished between two very different jobs:
sentences.zh: 到 2010 年代初，“我们有 webhooks”成为每个 API 登陆页面上的一个复选框，并且该复选框从未区分两个截然不同的作业：

blocks.html_en: • Trigger a side effect: send the receipt, start the build, ping the channel.

sentences.en: Trigger a side effect: send the receipt, start the build, ping the channel.
sentences.zh: 触发副作用：发送收据、开始构建、ping 通道。

blocks.html_en: • Keep a copy of the provider’s data correct: this customer deleted their payment method, so update it in your DB too.

sentences.en: Keep a copy of the provider’s data correct: this customer deleted their payment method, so update it in your DB too.
sentences.zh: 保持提供商数据的副本正确：该客户删除了他们的付款方式，因此也在您的数据库中更新它。

blocks.html_en: Job one is what webhooks were born for. Job two is what I was doing all three times, and job two is the one where every property webhooks lack (ordering, completeness, bootstrap, verifiability) is precisely the property you need.

sentences.en: Job one is what webhooks were born for.
sentences.zh: 第一项工作就是 webhook 的诞生。

sentences.en: Job two is what I was doing all three times, and job two is the one where every property webhooks lack (ordering, completeness, bootstrap, verifiability) is precisely the property you need.
sentences.zh: 工作二是我做了三次的事情，工作二是每个属性 webhooks 所缺乏的（排序、完整性、引导、可验证性）正是您需要的属性。

blocks.html_en: We picked the tool that was lying on the table in 2007, and then we spent fifteen years compensating.

sentences.en: We picked the tool that was lying on the table in 2007, and then we spent fifteen years compensating.
sentences.zh: 我们在 2007 年选择了摆在桌面上的工具，然后我们花了十五年的时间来弥补。

blocks.html_en: The valley

sentences.en: The valley
sentences.zh: 山谷

blocks.html_en: There’s a concept in evolutionary biology I can’t stop thinking about: the fitness landscape. Peaks are good designs, valleys are bad ones, and populations climb whatever slope they happen to be standing on. The trap is the local optimum: a small hill that’s better than its immediate surroundings, so evolution parks there, even when a much higher peak exists across the valley. Getting to the higher peak means crossing through designs that are temporarily worse, and evolution doesn’t do temporarily worse.

sentences.en: There’s a concept in evolutionary biology I can’t stop thinking about: the fitness landscape.
sentences.zh: 进化生物学中有一个概念让我无法停止思考：适应度景观。

sentences.en: Peaks are good designs, valleys are bad ones, and populations climb whatever slope they happen to be standing on.
sentences.zh: 高峰是好的设计，山谷是糟糕的设计，人们会爬上他们碰巧站在的任何斜坡。

sentences.en: The trap is the local optimum: a small hill that’s better than its immediate surroundings, so evolution parks there, even when a much higher peak exists across the valley.
sentences.zh: 陷阱是局部最优：一座比周围环境更好的小山，因此即使山谷中存在更高的山峰，进化也会停在那里。

sentences.en: Getting to the higher peak means crossing through designs that are temporarily worse, and evolution doesn’t do temporarily worse.
sentences.zh: 达到更高的顶峰意味着要跨越暂时更糟糕的设计，而进化不会暂时更糟糕。

blocks.html_en: Webhooks-for-replication are a local optimum, and the proof is the pile of workarounds on the valley floor: signature schemes, dedup stores, idempotent handlers, retry queues with exponential backoff on the provider side and dead-letter queues behind them, webhook logs with replay tooling because consumers keep asking for replays, and my 3 a.m. cron.

sentences.en: Webhooks-for-replication are a local optimum, and the proof is the pile of workarounds on the valley floor: signature schemes, dedup stores, idempotent handlers, retry queues with exponential backoff on the provider side and dead-letter queues behind them, webhook logs with replay tooling because consumers keep asking for replays, and my 3 a.m.
sentences.zh: 用于复制的 Webhooks 是局部最优，证据就是谷底的一堆解决方法：签名方案、重复数据删除存储、幂等处理程序、提供者端具有指数退避的重试队列和后面的死信队列、带有重播工具的 Webhook 日志（因为消费者不断要求重播），以及我的凌晨 3 点。

sentences.en: cron.
sentences.zh: 计划任务。

blocks.html_en: The pile has an economy on top of it. Svix exists so providers don’t have to build webhook delivery; Hookdeck exists so consumers don’t have to build webhook ingestion. AWS will sell you the valley as managed services, with EventBridge to ingest your SaaS partners’ events, SQS to queue them, and Lambda to retry your handler, and you get to assemble the pipeline yourself. And an entire industry of connector platforms (Fivetran, Airbyte, every “unified API” startup) is, at bottom, pseudo-CDC: change data capture reconstructed from webhooks and polled list APIs, one bespoke connector at a time, sold as a product. Inside a database, capturing changes is a solved problem: it’s called replication, and it works because there’s a log. Between companies, we rebuild it out of doorbells.

sentences.en: The pile has an economy on top of it.
sentences.zh: 这堆东西上面有一个经济。

sentences.en: Svix exists so providers don’t have to build webhook delivery; Hookdeck exists so consumers don’t have to build webhook ingestion.
sentences.zh: Svix 的存在是为了让提供商不必构建 webhook 交付； Hookdeck 的存在是为了让消费者不必构建 webhook 摄取。

sentences.en: AWS will sell you the valley as managed services, with EventBridge to ingest your SaaS partners’ events, SQS to queue them, and Lambda to retry your handler, and you get to assemble the pipeline yourself.
sentences.zh: AWS 将把整个山谷作为托管服务出售给您，使用 EventBridge 来摄取您的 SaaS 合作伙伴的事件，使用 SQS 对它们进行排队，使用 Lambda 来重试您的处理程序，然后您就可以自己组装管道。

sentences.en: And an entire industry of connector platforms (Fivetran, Airbyte, every “unified API” startup) is, at bottom, pseudo-CDC: change data capture reconstructed from webhooks and polled list APIs, one bespoke connector at a time, sold as a product.
sentences.zh: 整个连接器平台行业（Fivetran、Airbyte、每个“统一 API”初创公司）本质上都是伪 CDC：从 Webhooks 和轮询列表 API 重建的更改数据捕获，一次一个定制连接器，作为产品出售。

sentences.en: Inside a database, capturing changes is a solved problem: it’s called replication, and it works because there’s a log.
sentences.zh: 在数据库内部，捕获更改是一个已解决的问题：这称为复制，它之所以有效，是因为有日志。

sentences.en: Between companies, we rebuild it out of doorbells.
sentences.zh: 在公司之间，我们用门铃重建它。

blocks.html_en: My favorite workaround of them all is the local tunnel. Many providers ship a CLI like stripe listen that opens a tunnel to your laptop, because a webhook cannot reach localhost. Think about what that is: a product, built and maintained by the provider, reinvented multiple times, whose entire purpose is to work around the delivery direction of their own primitive. When multiple providers all need to ship a local tunnel so developers can develop, the primitive is answering the wrong question.

sentences.en: My favorite workaround of them all is the local tunnel.
sentences.zh: 其中我最喜欢的解决方法是本地隧道。

sentences.en: Many providers ship a CLI like stripe listen that opens a tunnel to your laptop, because a webhook cannot reach localhost.
sentences.zh: 许多提供商提供类似 Stripe Listen 的 CLI，它会打开通往笔记本电脑的隧道，因为 Webhook 无法到达本地主机。

sentences.en: Think about what that is: a product, built and maintained by the provider, reinvented multiple times, whose entire purpose is to work around the delivery direction of their own primitive.
sentences.zh: 想想那是什么：由提供商构建和维护的产品，经过多次重新发明，其全部目的是围绕其自己的原语的交付方向进行工作。

sentences.en: When multiple providers all need to ship a local tunnel so developers can develop, the primitive is answering the wrong question.
sentences.zh: 当多个提供商都需要提供本地隧道以便开发人员进行开发时，原语就回答了错误的问题。

blocks.html_en: None of this tooling is bad engineering; it’s excellent engineering. That’s what a local optimum looks like: so much excellent engineering poured into the valley floor that the valley becomes comfortable, and nobody looks up.

sentences.en: None of this tooling is bad engineering; it’s excellent engineering.
sentences.zh: 这些工具都不是糟糕的工程；这是出色的工程。

sentences.en: That’s what a local optimum looks like: so much excellent engineering poured into the valley floor that the valley becomes comfortable, and nobody looks up.
sentences.zh: 这就是局部最优的样子：大量优秀的工程涌入谷底，使山谷变得舒适，没有人抬头。

blocks.html_en: But some providers have looked up. Stripe retains thirty days of events and exposes /v1/events, an ordered, listable log, and recommends reconciling against it. WorkOS ships an Events API, an ordered cursor-paginated log, and their own docs recommend it over webhooks when data consistency matters. The log keeps escaping, and each escape mints its own bespoke cursor semantics, its own bootstrap story, no way to verify a replica, and no shared contract, but the direction is unmistakable. This is convergent evolution: unrelated organisms, same environmental pressure, same wing.

sentences.en: But some providers have looked up.
sentences.zh: 但一些提供商已经开始关注。

sentences.en: Stripe retains thirty days of events and exposes /v1/events, an ordered, listable log, and recommends reconciling against it.
sentences.zh: Stripe 保留三十天的事件并公开 /v1/events（一个有序的、可列出的日志），并建议对其进行协调。

sentences.en: WorkOS ships an Events API, an ordered cursor-paginated log, and their own docs recommend it over webhooks when data consistency matters.
sentences.zh: WorkOS 提供了一个事件 API、一个有序的游标分页日志，当数据一致性很重要时，他们自己的文档推荐使用它而不是 Webhooks。

sentences.en: The log keeps escaping, and each escape mints its own bespoke cursor semantics, its own bootstrap story, no way to verify a replica, and no shared contract, but the direction is unmistakable.
sentences.zh: 日志不断转义，每次转义都会产生自己定制的游标语义、自己的引导故事，无法验证副本，也没有共享合约，但方向是明确无误的。

sentences.en: This is convergent evolution: unrelated organisms, same environmental pressure, same wing.
sentences.zh: 这就是趋同进化：不相关的生物体，相同的环境压力，相同的翅膀。

blocks.html_en: The log exists everywhere, but the contract doesn’t.

sentences.en: The log exists everywhere, but the contract doesn’t.
sentences.zh: 日志无处不在，但合约却不存在。

blocks.html_en: Could it be better?

sentences.en: Could it be better?
sentences.zh: 还能更好吗？

blocks.html_en: Before reaching for a new design, it’s worth asking what any replacement would actually have to provide. My three integrations suggest the list: order, so changes can be applied without buffering; a way to start from nothing, so bootstrap isn’t a separate import racing the live events; deletes as data, so absence stops being the failure mode; resumability, so my downtime is my problem instead of a data-loss event; and some way to verify the result, so trust doesn’t decay into a 3 a.m. cron.

sentences.en: Before reaching for a new design, it’s worth asking what any replacement would actually have to provide.
sentences.zh: 在进行新设计之前，有必要询问任何替代品实际上必须提供什么。

sentences.en: My three integrations suggest the list: order, so changes can be applied without buffering; a way to start from nothing, so bootstrap isn’t a separate import racing the live events; deletes as data, so absence stops being the failure mode; resumability, so my downtime is my problem instead of a data-loss event; and some way to verify the result, so trust doesn’t decay into a 3 a.m.
sentences.zh: 我的三个集成建议了这个列表：顺序，因此可以在没有缓冲的情况下应用更改；一种从无到有的方式，因此 Bootstrap 并不是现场赛事中的单独导入；作为数据删除，因此缺席不再是故障模式；可恢复性，因此停机是我的问题，而不是数据丢失事件；以及验证结果的某种方式，这样信任就不会衰减到凌晨 3 点。

sentences.en: cron.
sentences.zh: 计划任务。

blocks.html_en: Measured against that list, the obvious candidates come up short. Polling the list APIs harder is the reconciliation cron promoted to a whole strategy: it can rebuild current state, but it burns rate limits discovering that mostly nothing changed, it says nothing about order, and a deleted object looks identical to an object that never existed. Managed delivery, whether that’s Svix on the provider’s side or EventBridge and SQS on mine, makes the pushes more reliable, but they are still pushes: still no bootstrap, still no verification, still notifications pretending to be a dataset. That path hardens the valley floor without climbing anywhere.

sentences.en: Measured against that list, the obvious candidates come up short.
sentences.zh: 与这份名单相比，明显的候选人都表现不佳。

sentences.en: Polling the list APIs harder is the reconciliation cron promoted to a whole strategy: it can rebuild current state, but it burns rate limits discovering that mostly nothing changed, it says nothing about order, and a deleted object looks identical to an object that never existed.
sentences.zh: 更难地轮询列表 API 是将协调 cron 提升为整个策略：它可以重建当前状态，但它会燃烧速率限制，发现几乎没有任何变化，它没有说明顺序，并且删除的对象看起来与从未存在的对象相同。

sentences.en: Managed delivery, whether that’s Svix on the provider’s side or EventBridge and SQS on mine, makes the pushes more reliable, but they are still pushes: still no bootstrap, still no verification, still notifications pretending to be a dataset.
sentences.zh: 托管交付，无论是提供商方面的 Svix 还是我方面的 EventBridge 和 SQS，都使推送更加可靠，但它们仍然是推送：仍然没有引导程序，仍然没有验证，仍然假装是数据集的通知。

sentences.en: That path hardens the valley floor without climbing anywhere.
sentences.zh: 这条路使谷底变得坚硬，无需攀登任何地方。

blocks.html_en: The third candidate is the one the providers keep half-building on their own: stop pushing altogether, and let the consumer read the log itself.

sentences.en: The third candidate is the one the providers keep half-building on their own: stop pushing altogether, and let the consumer read the log itself.
sentences.zh: 第三种候选方案是提供商自行半构建的候选方案：完全停止推送，让消费者自己读取日志。

blocks.html_en: Flip the arrow

content_html_zh:
第三次

我现在已经在三个不同的公司、三个不同的提供商构建了三次相同的系统。 它从来没有名字，也从未出现在路线图上，但它总是以同样的方式进行：有关您自己客户的真相存在于其他人的数据库中。 用户生活在身份提供商中，Stripe 中的订阅，发送电子邮件的任何内容的退回，而您的产品在本地需要这一事实。 因此，您订阅了 webhooks 并保留了一份副本。

第一次，我以为我正在构建一个端点：一个解析 JSON 并更新一行的路由，一个下午的工作。

下午变成了一周。 首先是签名验证，因为改变数据库的开放端点是一个漏洞。 然后是重复数据删除表，因为交付到达两次，文档高兴地称之为“至少一次”。 然后处理程序得到一个缓冲区，因为membership.created有时会出现在它指向的user.created之前。 然后是引导导入程序，因为 webhooks 只告诉您订阅后会发生什么，并且它会与实时事件竞争，因此它发展了一个锁定方案。 最后是协调 cron：这项工作会在凌晨 3 点抓取提供商的 API 列表，将它们与我们的表进行比较，并悄悄地修复不一致的内容。

我想诚实地了解那个 cron 是什么。 这是一份书面的认罪书。 它说：我不信任我构建的副本，我无法知道它什么时候出错，所以我每天晚上都会从头开始重新推导它，永远。

信任消失是有原因的。 漂移永远不会自行显现；我们是通过支持票找到的。 一位客户在几个月前取消了订单，而我们的数据库仍然显示处于活动状态；一些 customer.subscription.deleted 在 Stripe 和我们之间消失了，任何地方都没有注意到：不是他们的仪表板，它显示了重试并最终丢弃的交付，也不是我们的日志，它无法记录从未到达的请求。

这只是代码。 每个提供商还自带自己的仪表板。 三个提供程序、三个 Webhook 配置页面，每个页面都有自己的想法：如何注册端点、存在哪些事件、如何分隔测试和实时环境以及签名秘密所在的位置。 当出现问题时，调试就是一次游览：他们的交付日志在一个选项卡中，我们的日志在另一个选项卡中，第三个选项卡用于我当前怀疑的仪表板。 它们看起来都不一样，都必须进行检查。

当我第三次构建这个系统时，我已经不再假装了。 我预先对整个堆栈进行了预算（签名、重复数据删除、缓冲、引导程序、cron），在编写第三个重复数据删除表的过程中，我终于问了我应该第一次问的问题。

我到底要在这里重建什么？

通知不是数据

我正在重建一个有序的日志。 这些集成中的每一个都试图将通知流转回其来源的有序、完整、当前的历史记录。

这是荒谬的部分：历史存在。 它必须如此，因为它位于提供者内部；这就是他们呈现仪表板、事件页面和 Webhook 重播工具的方式。 提供者获取他们有序的日志，将其粉碎成单独的 HTTP POST，通过既不保证顺序也不保证交付的通道在我的端点处触发它们，然后我在我这边重新组装日志。 其他每个独立的消费者也是如此，每个人都有自己的错误。

这是一个拼图游戏，制造商有原始图片，将其剪碎，一次邮寄给我一块，在邮寄过程中丢失了一些，邮寄了两次，并且在盒子上没有打印任何内容。 当我组装的拼图与原始拼图不匹配时，他们的支持团队会问我缺少哪些拼图。 我不知道，这就是整个问题：没有任何东西表明存在差距。

这些都不是任何提供商的错误。 他们的 webhook 的工作方式与记录的完全一样。 问题在于 webhook 是什么：一个通知，“发生了一些事情，这里有一个关于它的帖子。” 通知是触发副作用的好方法，也是传输数据集的糟糕方法，在我们开始将它们用于第二件事的过程中，我们没有注意到我们已经换了工作。

这如何成为常态？

没有人决定这个。 “webhook”这个术语是由 Jeff Lindsay 在 2007 年创造的，早期的用途确实很合适：GitHub 的 post-receive hooks 启动 CI 构建，或者支付事件 ping 您的服务器，以便它可以通过电子邮件发送收据。 我们的工作是在事情发生时做一件事，为此，POST 是完美的：当忘记可以时，即发即忘也可以。

Webhook 之所以能够传播，是因为它们是提供商可以运送的最便宜的东西（一个 HTTP POST），也是消费者可以接收的最便宜的东西（您已经有一个 Web 服务器，所以您只需添加一条路由）。 到 2010 年代初，“我们有 webhooks”成为每个 API 登陆页面上的一个复选框，并且该复选框从未区分两个截然不同的作业：

  1. 触发副作用：发送收据、开始构建、ping 通道。
  2. 保持提供商数据的副本正确：该客户删除了他们的付款方式，因此也在您的数据库中更新它。

第一项工作就是 webhook 的诞生。 工作二是我做了三次的事情，工作二是每个属性 webhooks 所缺乏的（排序、完整性、引导、可验证性）正是您需要的属性。

我们在 2007 年选择了摆在桌面上的工具，然后我们花了十五年的时间来弥补。

山谷

进化生物学中有一个概念让我无法停止思考：适应度景观。 高峰是好的设计，山谷是糟糕的设计，人们会爬上他们碰巧站在的任何斜坡。 陷阱是局部最优：一座比周围环境更好的小山，因此即使山谷中存在更高的山峰，进化也会停在那里。 达到更高的顶峰意味着要跨越暂时更糟糕的设计，而进化不会暂时更糟糕。

用于复制的 Webhooks 是局部最优，证据就是谷底的一堆解决方法：签名方案、重复数据删除存储、幂等处理程序、提供者端具有指数退避的重试队列和后面的死信队列、带有重播工具的 Webhook 日志（因为消费者不断要求重播），以及我的凌晨 3 点。 计划任务。

这堆东西上面有一个经济。 Svix 的存在是为了让提供商不必构建 webhook 交付； Hookdeck 的存在是为了让消费者不必构建 webhook 摄取。 AWS 将把整个山谷作为托管服务出售给您，使用 EventBridge 来摄取您的 SaaS 合作伙伴的事件，使用 SQS 对它们进行排队，使用 Lambda 来重试您的处理程序，然后您就可以自己组装管道。 整个连接器平台行业（Fivetran、Airbyte、每个“统一 API”初创公司）本质上都是伪 CDC：从 Webhooks 和轮询列表 API 重建的更改数据捕获，一次一个定制连接器，作为产品出售。 在数据库内部，捕获更改是一个已解决的问题：这称为复制，它之所以有效，是因为有日志。 在公司之间，我们用门铃重建它。

其中我最喜欢的解决方法是本地隧道。 许多提供商提供类似 Stripe Listen 的 CLI，它会打开通往笔记本电脑的隧道，因为 Webhook 无法到达本地主机。 想想那是什么：由提供商构建和维护的产品，经过多次重新发明，其全部目的是围绕其自己的原语的交付方向进行工作。 当多个提供商都需要提供本地隧道以便开发人员进行开发时，原语就回答了错误的问题。

这些工具都不是糟糕的工程；这是出色的工程。 这就是局部最优的样子：大量优秀的工程涌入谷底，使山谷变得舒适，没有人抬头。

但一些提供商已经开始关注。 Stripe 保留三十天的事件并公开 /v1/events（一个有序的、可列出的日志），并建议对其进行协调。 WorkOS 提供了一个事件 API、一个有序的游标分页日志，当数据一致性很重要时，他们自己的文档推荐使用它而不是 Webhooks。 日志不断转义，每次转义都会产生自己定制的游标语义、自己的引导故事，无法验证副本，也没有共享合约，但方向是明确无误的。 这就是趋同进化：不相关的生物体，相同的环境压力，相同的翅膀。

日志无处不在，但合约却不存在。

还能更好吗？

在进行新设计之前，有必要询问任何替代品实际上必须提供什么。 我的三个集成建议了这个列表：顺序，因此可以在没有缓冲的情况下应用更改；一种从无到有的方式，因此 Bootstrap 并不是现场赛事中的单独导入；作为数据删除，因此缺席不再是故障模式；可恢复性，因此停机是我的问题，而不是数据丢失事件；以及验证结果的某种方式，这样信任就不会衰减到凌晨 3 点。 计划任务。

与这份名单相比，明显的候选人都表现不佳。 更难地轮询列表 API 是将协调 cron 提升为整个策略：它可以重建当前状态，但它会燃烧速率限制，发现几乎没有任何变化，它没有说明顺序，并且删除的对象看起来与从未存在的对象相同。 托管交付，无论是提供商方面的 Svix 还是我方面的 EventBridge 和 SQS，都使推送更加可靠，但它们仍然是推送：仍然没有引导程序，仍然没有验证，仍然假装是数据集的通知。 这条路使谷底变得坚硬，无需攀登任何地方。

第三种候选方案是提供商自行半构建的候选方案：完全停止推送，让消费者自己读取日志。

翻转箭头

这是思想实验。 如果我们不是让提供商告诉我们何时有新信息，而是询问提供商自上次检查以来它为我们提供了哪些新信息，该怎么办？

假设一个提供者为每个集合提供一个 URL，并且该 URL 返回一个有序的、光标寻址的全状态事件更改日志。 没有光标询问，您可以从头开始阅读，这是您的引导程序，没有单独的导入，也没有竞争。 用光标询问，您就可以从上次中断的地方继续。 您的整个同步状态就是该光标。

这些都不是异国情调的。这是一个分页的 GET。 但是回顾一下我下午的增长，看看它对堆栈做了什么：

  • 重复数据删除表消失了。 每个事件都携带对象的完整当前状态，因此应用一个事件是通过 id 键控的盲目更新插入，并且应用两次相同的事件会产生相同的结果。
  • 排序缓冲区消失了，因为日志已排序。
  • 引导导入程序及其锁定方案都消失了。 新消费者无需光标即可读取相同的提要，重播该集合，并直接在一个请求中进行实时更改。
  • 丢失删除是不可能的。 墓碑是日志中的一个事件，它会一直保留在那里，直到我阅读它为止。 我被取消的客户不能默默地保持活跃，因为缺席不再是失败模式。
  • 端点、签名和隧道从一开始就不存在。 每个连接都是消费者发起的，并且循环在 NAT 后面、笔记本电脑上或计划的作业中运行。

饲料还可以携带一件东西。 当读取到达日志末尾时，提供程序可以告诉您那里应该有什么：当前状态的计数和校验和，在您现在持有的光标处。 您比较两者，您知道您的副本是正确的，而不是假设它。 我的凌晨3点 cron，书面的忏悔，成为我在我想要安排一个比较时就已经做过的比较。

第四次

如果存在这样的提要，那么我第四次构建此系统将是一个循环：获取提要，让“upsert”将对象更新到我的数据库中，然后“delete”删除它，并保存最后一个光标。 那是二十行，没有路线，没有要轮换的秘密，没有队列，也没有 cron。 该副本带有自己的正确性证明，当有人询问哪些客户有有效订阅和退回电子邮件地址时，答案是跨本地表的 JOIN，不附加任何静默星号。

今天没有人提供这个服务。 这就是要点，也是重点。

我想看看这个想法是否能被准确地记录下来，所以我将其起草为一个协议：SCROLL，Synchronized Change Replication Over Line Logs 的缩写，位于 welidev.github.io/scroll。 从征求意见的意义上来说，这是 00 号草案。 它确定了提要、光标、流和轮询模式、检查点、逻辑删除和保留，并标记了我自己信心最低的地方。 它还不需要等待提供者，因为填充程序可以从任何提供者的现有 Webhook 和列表 API 中合成提要，这就是我计划找出设计错误的地方的方法。
